Title

Software Engineer - Real-Time Geospatial Mapping for Planetary Exploration

BELONG. CONNECT. GROW. with KBR.

Around here, we define the future. We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers. But we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

Description Of Work Effort

Join NASA Ames writing software to help explore the moon! Help us meet the emerging needs of Artemis, Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) and future Moon-to-Mars missions. Looking for a software engineer to assist with development of two coordinated work efforts:

M2M CSDS - the Moon to Mars Collaborative Science Data System
WITME - Web-Based Integrated Terrain Model Estimation tool

These tools provide a reusable, science-centric collaboration platform that enables distributed science teams to collectively visualize, analyze, and interpret mission data in support of time-critical decision making. They will prototype capability for uncertainty-aware fusion of orbital and surface terrain data for real-time operational decision support.

M2M CSDS and WITME both build on NASA Ames - developed collaborative data systems and science operations architectures matured through the Exploration Ground Data Systems (xGDS) research project and VIPER mission science operations.

M2M CSDS development will require the applicant to work closely with an active CLPS science team to populate the proof-of-concept M2M CSDS with mission relevant data. Software development will include an interactive, shared planning/replanning and execution monitoring capability that builds on design concepts developed for the Ames-led xGDS in a mature mission-proven environment. The work effort will include the integration of FedRAMP and NASA approved AI tools (e.g. Google Gemini) to provide summarization and search capabilities on the data sets and annotations deployed in M2M CSDS. These capabilities are anticipated to provide substantial benefits for supporting real-time science and operations (e.g. rapid initial generation of shift handover highlights that can be further augmented and edited by science team members).

WITME involves the development and application of statistically principled fusion methods to weight orbital and surface data by their uncertainties, and build unified 3D models with quantitative confidence estimates derived from these data. Specifically, the applicant will help develop effective user interfaces and displays to communicate confidence in terrain model data at different locations. This will enable mission teams to rapidly assimilate new terrain data, improving traverse planning and decision-making through a collaborative web-based interface.

Required Experience & Skills

**Must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident**

Web Development: Expertise in JavaScript including at least one common JavaScript MVC framework (e.g., Vue, React, Bootstrap, or Angular)

UI/UX Proficiency: experience with user-facing application design and implementation. Familiar with modern standards and best practices in UI design and development (responsive design, ADA compliance).
Proficient in utilizing server-side services, APIs and database tools and understanding how they interface with complex JavaScript applications.
JavaScript Mapping/Rendering: An understanding of 2D geographic mapping libraries such as OpenLayers, CesiumJS, Three, Leaflet, Google Maps API, etc
Geographic Map Projections: Familiarity with using different map projections and coordinate systems.
Geographic Map Services: Familiarity with services that provide map layers such as Google or Bing Maps, MapBox or any WMS data provider/ DEMs.
3D Graphics: Experience with 3D graphics, particularly as used with terrain mapping (e.g. DEMs) and a practical understanding of the underlying mathematical concepts used in graphics

Areas Of Desired Experience & Skills

AI Tools: Experience integrating AI tools into a user facing application.
Robotics: Interest in and understanding the needs of working with robots. Direct experience is a plus.
Domain Knowledge: Experience with mobility systems (air, water, or ground) to understand their operational complexities.
User-Centered Design: Ability to gather feedback from end-users and iteratively improve tool design based on that input.
GDAL: Familiarity with GDAL and GeoTIFF files.
Server side development skills: Python, Flask/Bottle, Docker, REDIS, PostGIS/ Postgres

CesiumJS
Vue
Webpack
ES6
Bootstrap 5

Application Timeline

Duties

Join our team as a Cleanup Site Manager and apply your technical expertise to some of the Northwest Region's most complex cleanup projects. In this senior-level role, you will manage a portfolio of contaminated site projects through investigation, design, and remediation. You will be responsible for applying engineering knowledge and sound judgment to ensure the cleanup actions for your projects protect both human health and the environment. You will be accountable for managing the scope and regulatory milestones for multiple complex projects with a high degree of independence. You will also be accountable for evaluating reasonable and necessary costs for projects that receive state remedial action grant funding. This opportunity requires that you proactively collaborate with other experienced engineers, geologists, scientists, and technical specialists to oversee your projects through cleanup to ultimately reach closure. Joining our team provides the opportunity to shape cleanup outcomes, innovate within established frameworks, and contribute to lasting environmental change. If you are ready to take on challenging projects that require both technical depth and strategic thinking, we encourage you to consider joining us.

What You Will Do

Serve as the principal engineer and project manager for complex cleanup sites to guide a portfolio of projects past investigation, through feasibility studies, into remedial design, and finally through cleanup action implementation.
Provide formal engineering oversight to ensure all formal project activities comply with the Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA), Sediment Management Standards (SMS), Sediment Cleanup User’s Manual (SCUM), and other applicable regulations, policies, and guidance documents.
Lead Key Site Meetings with Liable Parties to advance formal cleanup projects through MTCA stage-gates.
Conduct annual field visits for all assigned sites to observe investigation, monitoring, sampling, pilot testing, full scale remediation, and other cleanup activities; travel is required to complete these visits.
Review technical documents such as work plans, environmental assessments, remedial investigation reports, feasibility study reports, models, cleanup action plans, and remedial designs to ensure documents are complete, technically sound, and compliant with regulatory requirements.
Prepare clear and explicit directives to liable parties and the public through written communication, including letters, memos, technical reports, bulletins, and fact sheets.
Manage project scope, schedule, and data, including organizing electronic and physical records, ensuring required data submittals, and maintaining information in agency systems.
Oversee Washington State Remedial Action Grant (RAG) funding for assigned projects by reviewing payment requests progress reports (PRPRs) and approval/denial processes for reasonable and necessary costs.
Develop new Agreed Orders, Consent Decrees, and Enforcement Orders in partnership with Attorney General’s Office and in accordance with agency policies and procedures.
When necessary, develop and manage project support contracts in partnership with a Program Contracts Officer and in accordance with agency policies and procedures.
When necessary, provide environmental engineering expertise to colleagues, support review of complex Unit projects, and contribute to activities such as initial investigations, State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) reviews, or periodic reviews.

Learn more about what it is like to be an Engineer at the Department of Ecology

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Registration as a Professional Engineer in the state of Washington or another state based on registration requirements equivalent to those in Washington AND
Five years of experience in environmental engineering, which includes the following:

Communication and Professional Judgment – Ability to prepare clear, accurate, and directive written and verbal communication that supports sound technical decisions and conveys expectations to others.
Collaboration and Coordination – Skill in organizing and coordinating project information and activities with a range of internal and external parties to support progress and resolve complex issues.
Project Management – Ability to plan, prioritize, and guide project activities to meet milestones, regulatory requirements, and schedules.
Project Financial Skills – Ability to evaluate project costs, review consultant invoices, and understand the financial aspects of environmental engineering tasks.
Cleanup Project Implementation – Experience applying environmental laws, rules, and guidance (such as Model Toxics Control Act, Sediment Management Standards, and Sediment Cleanup User’s Manual, or similar) to move contaminated sites through cleanup processes and ensure regulatory compliance.
Environmental Cleanup Engineering – Ability to evaluate contamination data, assess remedial alternatives, and review technical documents that support the selection and approval of cleanup actions protective of human health and the environment.

NOTE:
Requirements for registration as a Professional Engineer in the state of Washington are eight years of professional experience (which may include up to four years of college-level engineering education) and successful completion of sixteen hours of professional licensing exams. Applicants qualifying through the licensing equivalency option must achieve registration as a Professional Engineer in the state of Washington within six months of appointment to this class.

NOTE:

Applicants are responsible for reviewing and ensuring they meet Washington's comity requirements before submitting application materials.

Licensing requirements can be found on the Washington State Board of Registration for Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors website: How To Get Your Professional Engineer License When Licensed in Another Jurisdiction.

Desired Qualifications

Technical Writing and Communication – Experienced in preparing clear, concise, and technically accurate reports, correspondence, and presentations to support well documented project decisions.
Meeting Facilitation and Engagement – Skilled with organizing and leading large project meetings with various groups to ensure discussions remain focused, productive, and result in actionable outcomes.
Environmental Sampling and Data Analysis – Experienced in applying mixed media sampling methods, laboratory analytical processes, and environmental data interpretation to ensure accurate evaluation of Site conditions.

Administering state and delegated federal programs including the Shoreline Management Act, State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA), the Coastal Zone Management Act, the Clean Water Act Section 401 Water Quality Certification Program, and wetland and floodplain management authorities.

It is essential that this position model the highest standards of personal, professional, and ethical conduct in support of efficient, effective, and accountable government.

You will work with dedicated colleagues, Tribal and community partners, and leaders across all levels of government to deliver lasting, meaningful benefits for people and places statewide.

As an Environmental Inspector of Underground Storage Tank (UST) systems, you will help protect Washington’s land, water, and air by ensuring underground storage tank systems are operated, installed, and closed in compliance with state and federal regulations. BELONG. CONNECT. GROW. with KBR.

Around here, we define the future. We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers. But we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

Description Of Work Effort

Join NASA Ames writing software to help explore the moon! Help us meet the emerging needs of Artemis, Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) and future Moon-to-Mars missions. Looking for a software engineer to assist with development of two coordinated work efforts:

M2M CSDS - the Moon to Mars Collaborative Science Data System
WITME - Web-Based Integrated Terrain Model Estimation tool

These tools provide a reusable, science-centric collaboration platform that enables distributed science teams to collectively visualize, analyze, and interpret mission data in support of time-critical decision making. They will prototype capability for uncertainty-aware fusion of orbital and surface terrain data for real-time operational decision support.

M2M CSDS and WITME both build on NASA Ames - developed collaborative data systems and science operations architectures matured through the Exploration Ground Data Systems (xGDS) research project and VIPER mission science operations.

M2M CSDS development will require the applicant to work closely with an active CLPS science team to populate the proof-of-concept M2M CSDS with mission relevant data. Software development will include an interactive, shared planning/replanning and execution monitoring capability that builds on design concepts developed for the Ames-led xGDS in a mature mission-proven environment. The work effort will include the integration of FedRAMP and NASA approved AI tools (e.g. Google Gemini) to provide summarization and search capabilities on the data sets and annotations deployed in M2M CSDS. These capabilities are anticipated to provide substantial benefits for supporting real-time science and operations (e.g. rapid initial generation of shift handover highlights that can be further augmented and edited by science team members).

WITME involves the development and application of statistically principled fusion methods to weight orbital and surface data by their uncertainties, and build unified 3D models with quantitative confidence estimates derived from these data. Specifically, the applicant will help develop effective user interfaces and displays to communicate confidence in terrain model data at different locations. This will enable mission teams to rapidly assimilate new terrain data, improving traverse planning and decision-making through a collaborative web-based interface.

Get in at the ground floor with our South Railroad Project — a construction-ready, open-pit heap leach project located on the world-class Carlin Trend in Nevada, one of the most prolific gold-producing regions on the planet. Join us at this pivotal stage and help bring Nevada's next gold mine to life.

Position Title: Environmental Coordinator

Position Summary

As Equinox Gold continues to grow, we are seeking an Environmental Coordinator to join our team. Duties

As an Environmental Inspector of Underground Storage Tank (UST) systems, you will help protect Washington’s land, water, and air by ensuring underground storage tank systems are operated, installed, and closed in compliance with state and federal regulations. Through inspections, technical assistance, and enforcement, you will play a critical role in reducing leaks from underground storage tanks and preventing soil, groundwater, and air contamination. This position blends field work, problem-solving, and collaboration -- using sound professional judgment to support compliance, educate regulated parties, and promote healthy communities and natural resources statewide.

As an Environmental Inspector - Underground Storage Tanks (UST)
, your duties will include:

Travel to various facilities to conduct UST inspections in accordance with EPA technical compliance guidance, independently applying professional judgment to identify violations and determine appropriate corrective actions.
Perform UST system installation, retrofit, and decommissioning inspections to ensure work meets regulatory and environmental protection standards.
Issue enforcement actions consistent with the UST Inspector Enforcement Manual and follow up with responsible parties to return facilities to compliance.
Investigate complaints of suspected leaking underground storage tanks, documenting findings and recommending next steps.
Provide technical assistance and education to UST owners, operators, contractors, and internal staff on UST regulations, forms, and compliance requirements.
Serve as a regional point of contact for external customers on UST-related questions and issues.
Coordinate with owners, operators, contractors, and local governments on complex UST projects, and contribute to special projects such as developing or updating guidance, tools, and resources for inspectors.
Maintain accurate and complete UST files and databases by reviewing submittals, documenting compliance data, and supporting performance measures related to UST compliance.
